Cautiously positive. The FOMC underscores strengthening activity and employment alongside continued, sizable accommodation (near‑zero policy rate and ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases). This stance aligns with modern New Keynesian guidance that policy should be forward‑looking and supportive until maximum employment is approached and inflation expectations are anchored (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). The explicit average‑inflation‑targeting framework announced in 2020 signals tolerance for a temporary overshoot to re‑center inflation around 2%, which the literature views as reinforcing credibility when inflation has undershot. The operational choices—maintaining a floor system with interest on reserves and an ON RRP facility—are consistent with Goodfriend’s analysis of implementation: they stabilize money market rates without implying a policy tightening. Continued QE and forward guidance, tools documented in Fed research and practice, work to compress term premia and support credit to households and businesses, especially via Treasury and agency MBS markets. Still, the statement flags virus‑related risks and uneven sectoral recovery, tempering the tone. Netting these, the communication is moderately optimistic rather than exuberant.
